name: Biceps femoris tendon
description: Distal tendon of the long and short heads, running down the posterolateral knee to the fibular head, with arms around the LCL and a short-head arm to the lateral tibia behind Gerdy's tubercle. Round and low signal on axial images, with the common fibular nerve just posteromedial.
variants_pitfalls: Several arms with fat or a little fluid between them at the fibular head are normal; call a tear only with discontinuity, retraction or avulsion.
Insertion variants (mostly tibial in about 10%, entirely tibial in about 1%) and anomalous slips can cause a snapping tendon; they are not avulsions.
A larger lateral fibular head fragment carries the biceps and LCL (cruciate injury in 89% of radiographic avulsions in one series); a small horizontal styloid flake is the arcuate sign.
With a biceps or fibular head avulsion the common fibular nerve is often pulled with it (16 of 18 surgical cases); trace it for displacement, edema or discontinuity.
Short-head edema in an ACL-injured knee is meaningful: biceps complex injuries, nearly all short head, were found in 72% of acutely unstable knees in one series.
